### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**5** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5fa9375ec8279a7ee9e779049c0e93661c1786a3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a881a71bdb11306aee78cdd08259eae106a188d2` — the merge of head `ae7fa514e5fccd5ed58307428b2783bbb3ce63c6` into base `5fa9375ec8279a7ee9e779049c0e93661c1786a3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a881a71bdb11306aee78cdd08259eae106a188d2 && git checkout a881a71bdb11306aee78cdd08259eae106a188d2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5fa9375ec8279a7ee9e779049c0e93661c1786a3 ae7fa514e5fccd5ed58307428b2783bbb3ce63c6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 5fa9375ec8279a7ee9e779049c0e93661c1786a3 && git merge --no-ff ae7fa514e5fccd5ed58307428b2783bbb3ce63c6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5fa9375ec8279a7ee9e779049c0e93661c1786a3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

Face: narrowing. The PR's two code paths decide no face on their own (`record-recognisers --template --paths` reads them `TIER_DEFAULT`); the line-initial `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and in `.changeset/30005-cross-closure-dataset-filter-keys.md` puts the review on the narrowing face, so the scope floor is every diff path outside the prose faces, both named above. PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no author note is owed. No `Contract-review-claim`, hold or record on this head on either thread at read time (PR thread: one docs-drift bot comment only). Card thread read: 6621257853 (triage), 6647296389 (seat claim), 6648301262 (os-dev report).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The narrowing itself (correct, as declared).** `runtime-gate.ts#buildRuntimeWriteSnapshotSet` now narrows `objects` through `runtime-gate.ts#narrowObjectsToWriteClosure` with a fifth limb, the set `runtime-gate.ts#datasetBoundObjectNames(args.type, item, args.context?.datasets)`: for a `dashboard` write, the `object` of every dataset named at `widgets[].dataset`; for a `report` write, the `object` of the dataset at `report.dataset` and at each `blocks[].dataset`; every other type answers the shared empty `NO_NAMES`. Those are exactly the positions the two rules read (`validate-widget-bindings.ts#validateWidgetBindings` reads `w.dataset` at L971 and judges `w.filter` at L1157; `validate-report-runtime-filter.ts#validateReportRuntimeFilters` reads `report.dataset` at L122 and `block.dataset` at L131 and judges both `runtimeFilter`s). Resolution goes through the carried, never-narrowed `datasets`, so a dangling name re-admits nothing. Applied in the same loop to baseline, candidate and the #22118 `stored` universe, all from the candidate item's bindings, so the verdict stays candidate MINUS baseline over one object universe. Judged right.
2. **What is newly refused (dashboard and report writes with a package scope in force, a bound dataset outside the closure).** The dev names two rule ids; the diff reaches six, all through the same "object absent, skip" exit that limb 5 removes:
   - `widget-filter-field-unknown` (named) — `validate-widget-bindings.ts#judgeDatasetFilterKeys` skip 1 (`!graph.get(object)`, L772-773) is no longer taken; an unknown key is an `error`.
   - `report-filter-field-unknown` (named) — same judge, `validate-report-runtime-filter.ts` L99-112, container and joined-block keys.
   - `widget-filter-field-not-included` (⛔ not named) — the judge's second clause (L791-797): a dotted key that resolves but whose prefix is not in the dataset's `include`, `error`, pushed at `validate-widget-bindings.ts` L1172.
   - `dashboard-filter-field-unknown` and `dashboard-filter-field-not-included` (⛔ not named), both `error`, and `dashboard-filter-field-unprovisioned` (warning) — the (a1) dashboard-level filter check at `validate-widget-bindings.ts` L1013-1021 takes the identical skip (`graph.get(datasetObject)`) off the same index and so also starts judging a cross-closure widget's inherited `globalFilters`/`dateRange` field. The default `dateRange` field is injected and stays `isUnjudgeable` (`object-graph.ts#isUnjudgeable`, kinds `unknowable`/`hop-untargeted`), so a stock board is not newly refused.
   Direction is right for all six (each key lands in the same `runtimeFilter` slot the door binds), but the changeset's "Now" paragraph and the PR body name only the two; the seat's prose check should have the four added in one sentence (③).
3. **Nothing the dataset door binds is refused by the design.** Read in `judgeDatasetFilterKeys`: an injected system column (`created_at`), a dotted hop that lands on an object the snapshot still lacks, and every operator key stay `isUnjudgeable` and are never reported; only the base object is re-admitted, so the dotted-hop skip is unchanged. The CONTROL case pins `status`, `estimate_hours: { $gte: 1 }` and `created_at` clean on both write types. One pre-existing exception reaches the new population — a bare dimension or measure name — judged in ③ (not a defect of this diff's design).
4. **Flow, list-view and dataset closure refusals unchanged.** `datasetBoundObjectNames` returns `NO_NAMES` for every `type` other than `dashboard`/`report` (L511), and `narrowObjectsToWriteClosure(objects, scope, NO_NAMES)` is the old four-limb predicate verbatim (limb 5 is `datasetBoundObjects.has(name)` on an empty set), so every other write type's snapshot is byte-for-byte the `main` snapshot: `flow-trigger-unknown-object`, `flow-input-unknown-object`, `list-view-object-outside-closure` and the closure fix line on `object-reference-unknown` are untouched. Pinned by the DARK case (flow on `showcase_task`; list view of `showcase_task` whose `chart.dataset` is the cross-package dataset) and by the "public four-limb" case.
5. **Public surface of `@objectstack/lint`: unchanged.** `narrowObjectsToPackageClosure(objects: readonly unknown[], scope: RuntimePackageScope | undefined): readonly unknown[]` keeps its signature and answer (delegates with `NO_NAMES`). `datasetBoundObjectNames` is `export`ed from the module for the unit pin only: `packages/lint/src/index.ts` L1165-1179 and `packages/lint/src/runtime.ts` L65-72 are named export lists (no `export *` from `runtime-gate.js`), the entries are tsup-bundled, and the module's `.d.ts` is not addressable through `exports` — shipped bytes, not a published accept set (contract-review.md). The three outside callers of the public function (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-object-extension-item.ts` L213, `packages/runtime/src/domains/new-similar-target.ts` L172, `ui/packages/app-shell/.../objectPickerClosure.ts`) see no change. No new rule id, error code or severity: the door's mapping of a gate `error` to `422 INVALID_METADATA` is the existing one. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is therefore right (nothing widened, the accept set narrowed); `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is right (a value an author could write — a filter key the object lacks — is now refused, AGENTS.md step 3 "a value refused … is `narrowed`"), and both lines are line-initial in the PR body and the changeset.
6. **The door is live for limb 5.** `packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.ts` L1300-1316 threads `type`, `packageScope` and a `context` carrying `datasets` (live + pending) into `runRuntimeAuthoringRules`, which builds its snapshots through `buildRuntimeWriteSnapshotSet` (L1267), so both the per-item publish and the package draft publish take the new limb; the dev's door measurement (422 at `dashboards[0].widgets[0].filter.no_such_field`; `status` saves; `main` lint publishes the bad key) agrees with the read.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/30005-cross-closure-dataset-filter-keys.md`: `'@objectstack/lint': minor` (lint is a released package: `packages/lint/package.json` has no `private` field, version 18.3.0, three `exports` entries), `**BREAKING**` banner present, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` line-initial, exactly one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription) …` marker. Against AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3: kind `narrowed` takes at least `minor` on the moved package — `minor` ✓; `(narrowing)` is BREAKING — banner ✓; a breaking changeset states its ADR-0087 disposition in writing — ✓; no spec key, export or config field is removed or renamed, so no FROM → TO migration line and no `retiredKey()` tombstone is owed, and the "What an author does" paragraph is the right prescription (name a real field). `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` pushes breaking changes to `minor` outside pre-mode, so `minor` + banner is the consistent spelling. The dev's declared level (minor + BREAKING + adr-0087 not-required) is consistent with the changeset and with the diff. `Check Changeset`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are `success` on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **`Skills-docs:` line — present, wrong spelling, and not true as written (seat REWORK item, prose face).** The allowed spellings are `updated here | follow-up owed — FILES | follow-up #N | none — REASON` (pm-dispatch SKILL.md L313; `updated here` covers "`skills/**` or the docs"). The PR body reads `Skills-docs: none in \`skills/**\`, which teaches neither rule nor the closure. \`content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx\` names the closure's four limbs and not the fifth…` — a `none` whose own sentence names a docs page this diff makes stale. The page is now false: `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx` L735-739 states the fourth door "narrows that context to the written item's **package closure** — the written package, its declared dependencies, and unconditionally both platform/system objects and rows carrying no package provenance (#9612)", which for a dashboard or report write no longer describes the snapshot (the bound datasets' base objects are carried too). Correct line: `Skills-docs: follow-up owed — content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx` (the seat files the card and rewrites it to `follow-up #N` before ACCEPT), or the one sentence added to that paragraph in this PR with `Skills-docs: updated here`. The dev already handed the page to the seat in the Acceptance notes and the report's `out_of_scope_findings`; the declaration line has to say so in the template's words. Outside the four contract faces; does not move this verdict.
2. **Dev flag — "#30006 meets a wider population": a real author-facing regression, judged acceptable here, with two conditions for the seat.** Scenario: runtime package `app.sales` (no dependency on the showcase) builds a dashboard on `showcase_task_metrics`, which declares a dimension `{ name: 'state', field: 'status' }`; the widget carries `filter: { state: 'done' }`. At run time `dataset-filter-field-binding.ts` L28-29 and L142 bind `state` to the dimension's `sql`, so the tile renders. On `main` the gate skipped (object absent) and the board published; on this head `widget-filter-field-unknown` refuses it `422` at `dashboards[0].widgets[0].filter.state`, because `validate-widget-bindings.ts` L1157-1168 has no dimension skip (the report rule has one at `validate-report-runtime-filter.ts` L101; neither rule skips a measure name). So yes: a body the door binds, that published before, is refused after. Why not a must-fix of this PR: the spec declares no dimension- or measure-key capability for these filters (`dashboard.zod.ts` L1182 "Presentation-scope filter (runtimeFilter)", `report.zod.ts` L454/L602 "Render-time scope filter"), so no declared capability is taken away at the consumer; the refusal is the rule's own pre-existing verdict on every in-closure dataset (the #30006 filer measured it there), and route 1's contract is precisely "the cross-closure verdict equals the in-closure one" (pinned); the owning card #30006 is serial behind this card on the same seat. Conditions: (a) the seat dispatches #30006 so both changesets ride the same release train — the window between the two landings is the only one in which a cross-closure author meets the refusal with no fix in sight; (b) the changeset's "Accepted, as before" list is not complete for a BREAKING-note reader: one sentence that a bare dimension or measure name is refused on a cross-closure dataset as it already is inside the closure, tracked by #30006, belongs there (prose face, seat's sentence check).
3. **Dev flag — dotted keys.** Confirmed in code: only the base object is re-admitted; a hop onto an object the snapshot lacks is `unknowable` and `isUnjudgeable`, never a finding. The changeset says so.
4. **Dev flag — HTTP status; do the refusal tests assert `code` and `status`?** No. The nine committed cases are lint-layer and assert `rule`, `path` and `severity: 'error'`; a lint finding carries no `code`/`status` (the envelope is the door's). The door mapping of these two rule ids to `422 INVALID_METADATA` is pinned in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.dashboard-dataset-publish-gate.test.ts` L435-484, but with no package closure in force; the card's pin "refused 422 at the widget path" under a closure was measured at the door (report 6648301262) and not committed, because the claim's file surface stopped at `packages/lint`. Under review-checklist "拒收用例 ⇒ `code`+`status` 最低断言" this is the seat's call: waive on the existing envelope pins plus the measured reading, or widen the file surface by one `describe` in that metadata-protocol test (a runtime-package dashboard on a cross-package dataset, `status`/`code` asserted). Not a contract-face must-fix.
5. **Unnamed rule ids (①.2).** `widget-filter-field-not-included`, `dashboard-filter-field-unknown`, `dashboard-filter-field-not-included`, `dashboard-filter-field-unprovisioned` now also reach cross-closure dashboards. Same direction, same door binding; the changeset should name them (prose face).
6. **Dev's out-of-scope dogfood red** (`test/update-by-id-refusal-order.dogfood.test.ts`, 404 where 403 is pinned) reproduced with lint at `origin/main` — not this diff; the report's dedupe words are there for the seat to file. The `dogfood_battery` field is pinned to this head, full, with the one red explained; noted for the seat's `!`/narrowing check.
7. **Check-runs at read time (2026-11-05 ~03:00Z):** `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `PR-body guards` are `success`; `Type Check · workspace/source gates/debt ledger/consumer gates`, `Type Check UI`, `Build Core`, `Test Core (1-8/8)`, `Test UI (1-16/16)`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards` still `in_progress`. The queue entry waits for all-green (contract-review.md ②); this record does not stand in for it.
8. **`open_questions`: []** — nothing to answer.

### ④ Design judgment

- **`packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts` — route 1 over route 2, holds against the code it cites and the card.** The card asks for one of two routes with a reason, and forbids refusing a key the door binds. The door (`dataset-filter-field-binding.ts` for `queryDataset`) resolves a cross-package dataset's filter against that dataset's own object with no closure in force; route 1 hands the two rules exactly that object and changes no rule, so the gate's universe for the filter keys is the door's. Route 2 would owe the cross-closure reference its own verdict, which the card's third pin (a good key still publishes) forbids refusing, and a non-refusing verdict would still leave the keys unjudged unless the object were brought in anyway — the dev's reasoning is right. Keying limb 5 on the written TYPE rather than on "any dataset reference" is the right boundary: the DARK case shows the alternative — a list view's `chart.dataset` re-admitting the very object the view lists would wave `list-view-object-outside-closure` through. Positions read agree with the rules' positions one for one; the dangling-dataset and no-datasets exits are right; applying the same set to all three passes keeps candidate MINUS baseline a single question. The public function's four-limb answer is preserved by delegation rather than by a second copy of the predicate — one implementation, as the closure ruling (#9612) requires.
- **`packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.package-closure.test.ts` — the pins carry the scenario.** New top-level `describe` in the component's existing harness (ruling 6583487846). LIT cases assert the exact finding list (`[rule, path]` pairs) for the filer's repro, the report twin and the joined container+block; the CONTROL case covers field, operator and injected-column keys on both write types; the scoped-equals-whole-collection equality is the strongest statement of route 1's contract; the dangling-dataset, DARK and public-four-limb cases pin what must not move; the unit pin reads both positions and the `view` exit. Ablation (limb 5 disabled through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, blob hashes recorded, restored to HEAD): 4 red / 5 green, the five green being the controls and pins that must not depend on the limb — the right split. The `datasetBoundObjectNames` export exists for this file only and matches the module's existing convention (`buildRuntimeWriteSnapshotSet`).
- **Must-fix defects on the contract faces: none.** The two correct declaration lines are `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`; the `Skills-docs:` line must be rewritten by the dev or seat as in ③.1 before ACCEPT (prose face).
